segments.text: Tuesday morning. A supplier you trust sends an invoice. Same logo. Same wording. ... It looks exactly like your supplier. The bank details are not theirs.

segments.scene: why filters miss it and our client
segments.text: The email is real. It comes from your supplier's own mailbox, so every check your filter runs, passes. In South Africa, digital banking fraud cost two point four one billion rand in twenty twenty-five. One of our own clients was sent five hundred and thirty-three phishing emails in thirty days. Their filter caught every one. The ones no filter can catch come from someone you trust.

Forward it to Is It Legit, and the report fills in live. Before any AI sees the mail, our checks extract text hidden from the reader, written to steer an AI assistant to classify the message as safe. It flags a reply address that goes somewhere else, and a link that shows one address and goes to another. Every finding comes with its evidence.

Businesses register who they really are on the Protect page: their trading names, their domains, their bank accounts, and their logo for SAM 3.1 to compare against mail. Every check is tracked in the organisation's cases console, and the first advice never changes: phone the number in your own records. In the Hawarden case, the appeal court ruled a five and a half million rand loss could have been avoided by verifying the account details.

segments.scene: trust network alerts, monitor and badges (draft placeholders)
segments.text: It works both ways. When someone checks a fake that uses your name, you are alerted. Every night, the monitor hunts lookalike login and payment sites, and hands you a takedown pack. Your signature badge and website seal are drawn live, and refuse to vouch on a counterfeit domain.

Under the hood, five Meta models work inside a strict safety contract. Untrusted content stays inside delimited blocks. Critical evidence sets a deterministic floor no model can lower, and every claim must cite an Evidence ID. Even voice notes are decoded in-Worker: a three-second Opus note in {fact.benchNoteOurs}, against FFmpeg's {fact.benchNoteFfmpeg}.

We hold our own models to the same standard: verify, don't assume. Loupe, our fine-tune of Muse Glimmer thirty B, trained on {fact.trainLines} lines in {fact.trainTime}. On held-out pages it caught {fact.lureRecallOf}, with {fact.falseAlarmsOf} false alarms, in {fact.latency}. We show its weak spot too: it names the lure type right about sixty-three and a half percent of the time.
Built in under two weeks by one operator and nine AI lanes. Your filter protects your inbox. We protect you from everyone else's. Is It Legit, at app.isitlegit.co.za.
